units.title: あいさつ
units.note: `こんにちは` (konnichiwa) is hello during the day, `おはようございます` (ohayō gozaimasu) good morning, `こんばんは` (konbanwa) good evening. `すみません` (sumimasen) means both "excuse me" and "sorry": the most useful word in Japan. Japanese usually leaves out "I" and "you"; add `さん` (san) after other people's names, never your own.

units.title: 雑談
units.note: `好きです` (suki desu) means "I like it"; the thing you like takes `が` (ga): `ラーメンが好きです`. `大好き` (daisuki) is "really like, love". `～ね` (ne) at the end invites agreement, like "isn't it?".

units.note: `分かりません` (wakarimasen) means "I don't understand". `もう一度` (mō ichido) is "once more" and `ゆっくり` (yukkuri) "slowly". `～が痛いです` (ga itai desu) says what hurts. Emergency numbers in Japan: 110 for police, 119 for an ambulance or fire.
